A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mess3 transformer study. All 15 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original transformer experiments, including attention and representation analyses, architectural comparisons using validation KL divergence, and PCA results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds training trajectories, comparisons with random initialization, and four-layer representation analyses.

M1.justification: The constrained belief updates, spectral mechanism, attention decomposition, and training objective remain unchanged. Four-layer transformers are additional evaluation configurations; no new proposed algorithm or component is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions study next-token prediction on the same three-state, three-symbol Mess3 HMM family. The added analyses reuse existing parameter conditions without introducing another dataset, task, domain, or input environment.

E2.justification: v2 adds randomly initialized transformers as explicit baselines for representation-fit comparisons in Figures A3, A4, and A6. The existing comparisons with theoretical predictions and alternative architectural configurations remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds checkpoint-based evaluations normalized to initialization and linear-regression evaluations across eight residual-stream stages of four-layer models. These substantially extend the evaluation design beyond v1's existing fits and one-to-three-layer KL sweep. Appendix B's training settings remain unchanged. Figure 4 also reverses two reported alpha labels without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figures A3–A6 add substantial analyses of whether geometric alignment develops during training and how constrained versus full belief representations evolve through deeper networks. The original embedding-discrepancy analysis, architectural sufficiency tests, and PCA dimensionality analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these experiments. The added MSE plots report point estimates without changing uncertainty-reporting practices; the original cross-validation comparisons remain.

E6.justification: Figures A3–A6 add training trajectories, trained-versus-random errors, and four-layer geometry results. For example, Figure A4 newly reports constrained-Mid and full-Post MSEs of 5.1e-4 and 8.5e-5 for x=0.15, alpha=0.6. Existing KL results and all PCA-table values are retained. Figure 4 swaps alpha=0.2 and 0.6 labels on its x=0.15 rows, changing their reported condition assignments.

T1.justification: The mathematical substance of Equations (1)–(20) and Appendix A is retained; appendix equations are renumbered from A1–A7 to 21–27. Added spectral intuition and the recurrent-versus-parallel diagram explain existing mathematics without introducing a new theorem, proof, or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction explicitly identify single-layer attention as the primary scope and add the claim that the mechanism extends to deeper networks. The abstract also shifts emphasis from explaining gradient descent to explaining architectural constraints. The three principal contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 expands the local-information rationale for constrained updates and interprets the new controls and depth analyses as evidence of learned geometry followed by refinement toward full beliefs. Limitations now discuss the tested four-layer models, while retaining the original restrictions concerning Mess3 and natural-language applicability.

D1.justification: Section 3 adds a link to an analysis notebook, providing code-access information absent from v1. Appendix B retains the existing architecture, optimizer, training budget, and sequence-generation details.

R1.justification: The underlying cited works and positioning relative to feature geometry, circuit analysis, and computational mechanics remain unchanged. v2's Shalizi and Crutchfield 2001a/2001b entries duplicate the same work already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v2 condenses related-work and methodology prose, expands intuition in Sections 4.3–4.4, updates scope statements, and adds appendix headings and an Impact Statement. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the conceptual diagram A1 and four analytical figures A3–A6, alongside a document-wide change to ICML formatting. Original Figures 5–7 become A2, A7, and A8; Table I becomes Table 1. Figure 4's parameter labels are revised, while most original graphical content is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through quantitative residual-geometry comparisons with random initialization and across layers, supplementing v1's existing circuit fits and KL tests. Clearer explanations and the analysis-code link also help. These gains are tempered by overinterpretation: Section 4.3 describes reductions as orders of magnitude although some Figure A4 improvements are only severalfold, and Figure A6's claimed crossover immediately after the first MLP is not universal in its plots.
